evidence.reason: The baseline accounting at lines 99-101 intersects mapped baseline debt only with the current row's uncovered intervals. When the current row is unmeasurable (lines None or disposition unsupported/ambiguous), its uncovered list is empty, so remaining is empty and all mapped debt is added to baseline_T1_reviewed_since; nothing here records that current object as unresolved (the unresolved test at lines 91-94 only examines the baseline row, not a measurable baseline row whose current object is unmeasurable/missing). That can yield surviving_T1_debt 0 plus empty unresolved_baseline_objects and a baseline-zero/pending status even though the debt was never actually shown reviewed. Treating unmeasurable debt as progress contradicts the existing unresolved-object accounting and the tighten-only baseline semantics (contract item 11). The finding targets implementation of existing intended behavior, not a new requirement.
